identity.title: Fast, Collimated Outflow in the Western Nucleus of Arp 220

paper_type_evidence.quote: The outflow, seen in HCN (1–0) by ALMA, is compact and collimated, with extension $\lesssim$ 120 pc.

evidence.quote: At a luminosity distance of 77 Mpc (z = 0.018126)

question.value: Is there a spatially and spectrally resolved molecular outflow in the western nucleus of Arp 220, and what are its properties and driving mechanism?

evidence.quote: Here, we present the first spatially and spectrally resolved image of the fast collimated molecular outflow in the western nucleus of Arp 220.

findings_qualitative.value: Outflow is bipolar along the disk minor axis, accelerates away from disk, and is also seen in CO (weaker) and dust continuum with alpha≥2

evidence.quote: The extended emission to the north and south has $\alpha \geq 2$ indicating that dust emission likely represents the dominant continuum component.

evidence.quote: We identify this emission as tracing a bipolar outflow from the disk.
